questions.stemHtml: ADH exerts its effects on the collecting ducts of the kidney. Which of the following best characterizes ADH activity, as depicted in the Image?

options.label: C
options.text: Binds at F and activates GI-mediated cyclic adenosine monophosphate cascade

options.label: D
options.text: Binds at F and activates Gs-mediated cyclic adenosine monophosphate cascade

questions.answerText: Binds at F and activates Gs-mediated cyclic adenosine monophosphate cascade
questions.solutionHtml:
Binds at F and activates Gs-mediated cyclic adenosine monophosphate cascade
  • ADH binds V2 receptors on the basolateral side of the principal cell and activates a Gs-mediated cyclic adenosine monophosphate cascade.
  • The final result is that aquaporin transmembrane channels, previously sequestered within intracellular vesicles, are mobilized to the luminal surface of the cells.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 666.

questions.stem: In response to an increase in GFR, the proximal tubule and the loop of Henle demonstrate an increase in the rate of Na+ reabsorption. This phenomenon is called ___
questions.solutionHtml:
Glomerulo tubular balance
  • One of the most basic mechanisms for controlling tubular reabsorption is the intrinsic ability of the tubules to increase their reabsorption rate in response to increased tubular load (increased tubular inflow).
    • This phenomenon is referred to as glomerulotubular
    • Thus, glomerulotubular balance refers to the fact that the total rate of reabsorption increases as the filtered load increases, even though the percentage of GFR reabsorbed in the proximal tubule remains relatively constant at about 65 percent.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 331.

questions.stemHtml: The glomerulus is a unique vascular structure consisting of a capillary bed interposed between two arterioles: the afferent and efferent arterioles. Image shows features such as, Select the incorrect:-

options.label: D
options.text: Receives blood supply from an efferent arteriole

questions.answerText: Receives blood supply from an efferent arteriole
questions.solutionHtml:
Receives blood supply from an efferent arteriole
  • Receives blood supply from an afferent arteriole.
  • The given Images shows Glomerulus (red), Bowman's capsule (blue), and proximal tubule (green).


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall, 14th Edition, Page No. 331

questions.stem: The glomerular capillary membrane has a structure similar to membranes of other capillaries in the body including capillaries in the brain. Select the correct difference between the glomerular capillary membrane and other capillary membranes?

options.label: A
options.text: The glomerular capillary membrane has three layers instead of two layers

options.label: B
options.text: Endothelium of the capillary; basement membrane; the layer of epithelial cells (podocytes)

options.label: C
options.text: Endothelium of the capillary; the layer of epithelial cells (podocytes)

questions.solutionHtml:
Only C correct
  • The glomerular capillary membrane is similar to that of other capillaries, except that it has three (instead of the usual two) major layers: (1) the endothelium of the capillary; (2) a basement membrane; and (3) a layer of epithelial cells (podocytes) surrounding the outer surface of the capillary basement membrane.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall, 14th Edition, Page No. 331-32

questions.stem: The glomerular basement membrane of the kidney is the basal lamina layer of the glomerulus. The glomerular endothelial cells, the glomerular basement membrane, and the filtration slits between the podocytes perform the filtration function of the glomerulus, separating the blood in the capillaries from the filtrate that forms in Bowman's capsule. Select the correct:

options.label: A
options.text: BM contains heparan sulfate adjacent to podocytes

options.label: B
options.text: BM contains chondroitin sulfate adjacent to endothelial cells

options.label: C
options.text: Impaired glomerular filtration membrane function is nephrotic syndrome

questions.solutionHtml:
All correct
  • Options A, B, and C are correct
  • The glomerular basement membrane of the kidney is the basal lamina layer of the glomerulus. The glomerular endothelial cells, the glomerular basement membrane, and the filtration slits between the podocytes perform the filtration function of the glomerulus, separating the blood in the capillaries from the filtrate that forms in Bowman's capsule.


    • Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall,14th Edition, Page No.332.

questions.stem: Podocytes are cells in Bowman's capsule in the kidneys that surround the capillaries of the glomerulus. Podocytes make up the epithelial lining of Bowman's capsule, Select the incorrect:

options.label: A
options.text: Essential component of the filtration membrane

options.label: C
options.text: Nephrin protein is helpful in ultrafiltration with podocytes

questions.solutionHtml:
Incorrect C
  • Options A, B, and C are correct
  • Podocytes are cells in Bowman's capsule in the kidneys that wrap around the capillaries of the glomerulus.
  • Podocytes make up the epithelial lining of Bowman's capsule, the third layer through which filtration of blood takes place.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall, 14th Edition, Page No.334

questions.stemHtml: The glomerular filtration membrane contains specific apertures for the movement of selective solutes across the filtration membrane as shown in the image.Select the incorrect:-

options.label: A
options.text: Fenestrations are round or ovoid transcellular holes in the endothelium in organs with a high rate of exchange.

options.label: B
options.text: Fenestrations are round or ovoid transcellular holes in the visceral layer of the Bowman capsule

options.label: C
options.text: Slit pores are spaces between the pedicles on the glomerular basement membrane

options.label: D
options.text: Water, glucose, amino acids, and other chemicals pass as they become renal filtrate.

questions.answerText: Fenestrations are round or ovoid transcellular holes in the visceral layer of the Bowman capsule
questions.solutionHtml:
Fenestrations are round or ovoid transcellular holes in the visceral layer of the Bowman capsule
  • Fenestrations are round or ovoid transcellular holes in the endothelium in organs with a high rate of exchange occur as in glomerulus in nephrons.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall, 14th Edition, Page No.332.

questions.stem: Endothelial cells line the capillaries in Bowman's capsule. Capillaries form the glomerulus. Physiologists determined the presence of a specific gap between two endothelial cells in capillaries.Select the correct:
questions.solutionHtml:
70-90 nm
  • The specific gap between two endothelial cells in capillaries is 70-90 nm.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall,14th ,Page No. 332.

questions.stemHtml: A child of age 7 years was taken to the hospital with presentations of edema of the face, and legs, and proteinuria. The physician recommended prednisolone therapy for one month initially but found that manifestations were nonresponsive to the steroid treatment.Later on, a Kidney biopsy reported the presence of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.Select the incorrect?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mutation NPHS1 gene
  • The mutation NPHS2 gene causes a deficiency of podocin.
  • Kidney biopsy shows a light micrograph of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, hilar variants, and PAS stain.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall, 14th Edition,Page No. 331.

questions.stem: The visceral epithelium in Bowman's capsule is the inner layer of cells. Its cells are highly specialized and called podocytes. These have foot processes called pedicels.Select the incorrect?

options.label: B
options.text: Slits are covered by slit diaphragms

questions.solutionHtml:
Slits are 35 nm wide
  • Normal width is 25 nm in slits
  • Each podocyte has many foot processes, which interdigitate to form filtration slits. The slits are approximately 25 nm wide and each is closed by an extremely thin process called slit diaphragms which bridge the slits between the pedicels.

 




Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall, 14th Edition, Page No. 333.

questions.stem: The glomerular filtration membrane undertakes a function of ultrafiltration to form glomerular filtrate in the space of Bowman's capsule. Physiologists reported selective permeability of the Glomerular filtration membrane. Select the incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Neutral substances which are 4 nm are freely filtered

options.label: B
options.text: Neutral substances which are 8 nm are not filtered

options.label: C
options.text: Neutral substances between 4 to 8 nm are freely filtered

options.label: D
options.text: Neutral substances between Between 4 nm and 8 nm have permeability inversely proportional to the diameter.

questions.answerText: Neutral substances between 4 to 8 nm are freely filtered
questions.solutionHtml:
Neutral substances between 4 to 8 nm are freely filtered
  • Neutral substances between 4 to 8 nm are not freely filtered. Their permeability is inversely proportional to the diameter.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall,14th Edition, Page No. 333.

questions.stem: Glomerular filtration membrane is effective in ultrafiltration. Physiologists observed that filtration of negatively charged molecules is comparatively more difficult than that of positively charged molecules.Select the correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Presence of Sialoproteins on the filtering membrane

options.label: C
options.text: Positively charged proteins on the filtering membrane

questions.answerText: Presence of Sialoproteins on the filtering membrane
questions.solutionHtml:
Presence of Sialoproteins on the filtering membrane
  • The presence of negatively charged sialoproteins on the filtering membrane is the correct statement.
  • Sialoproteins in the glomerular capillary wall are negatively charged, and the negative charges repel negatively charged substances in the


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.5-11, Guyton and Hall

questions.stem: Adolescent in age 15 years was taken to a nephrologist for manifestations of lethargy, nausea, loss of appetite, and passing red-colored urine past 3 months. Examination and tests revealed the presence of Alport syndrome. Select the correct option?

options.label: A
options.text: Deficiency of Collagen IV in basal lamina in Bowman capsule

questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • In the case of the 15-year-old adolescent, lethargy, nausea, loss of appetite, and passing red-colored urine are likely symptoms of kidney damage and dysfunction. The diagnosis of Alport syndrome was confirmed through genetic testing or a kidney biopsy, which showed characteristic changes in the basement membranes of the kidneys.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology,,14th Edition, Page Number 339.

questions.stem: Benign familial hematuria is an autosomal dominant condition. It manifests as nonprogressive isolated microscopic hematuria that does not result in renal failure. Patient of age 23 years presented with the manifestations of Benign familial hematuria past several months as reported by relatives in history. Select the correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Mutation in COL4A3 or COL4A4 gene

options.label: C
options.text: Patients remain asymptomatic in most cases

questions.solutionHtml:
Only Incorrect B
  • This condition results in basement membrane nephropathy.
  • In the case of the 23-year-old patient, the presence of benign familial hematuria is suggested by the reported history of isolated microscopic hematuria over several months. Diagnosis of the condition is typically made by ruling out other causes of hematuria, such as infections, kidney stones, or malignancies.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology,, 14th Edition, Page Number 339.

questions.stem: A male patient of 58 years reported lethargy, frothy urine, weakness, and passing-blood coloured urine past 2 months. Examination and tests confirmed the case of Fibrillary glomerulonephritis. Select the incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Fibrillary deposits in the BM of glomeruli

options.label: B
options.text: Fibrils are made of amyloid proteins

questions.answerText: Fibrils are made of amyloid proteins
questions.solutionHtml:
Fibrils are made of amyloid proteins
  • In the case of the 58-year-old male patient, the lethargy, frothy urine, weakness, and passing blood-colored urine are likely related to the kidney dysfunction caused by fibrillary glomerulonephritis. The diagnosis was confirmed through examination and tests, such as a kidney biopsy, which showed the characteristic deposits of fibrils in the glomeruli.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall,14th Edition, Page Number 339.

questions.stem: Patients at the age of 23 years presented with signs of the tetrad of changes in the nails, knees, and elbows, and the presence of iliac horns. The diagnosis was Nail-patella syndrome.Select the incorrect?
questions.solutionHtml:
All incorrect
  • In the case of the 23-year-old patient, the presence of the tetrad of changes in the nails, knees, and elbows, as well as the iliac horns, is suggestive of nail-patella syndrome.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall,14th Edition, Page Number 339.

questions.stemHtml: The image below depicts types of cells that together constitute a specific tissue in the nephron. Select the name of the tissue from the list below?
questions.solutionHtml:
Juxtaglomerular apparatus
  • The renin in kidney extracts and the bloodstream is produced by the juxtaglomerular cells (JG cells).
  • These epithelioid cells are located in the media of the afferent arterioles as they enter the glomeruli.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 1616-1617.

questions.stem: Kidneys possess a Tubuloglomerular feedback mechanism. It senses the rate of glomerular filtration to the concentration of sodium chloride in tubule fluid at the macula densa and autoregulation of GFR and renal blood flow. Select the best-suited components of the Tubuloglomerular feedback mechanism?

options.label: C
options.text: Anatomical arrangements of the juxtaglomerular complex

questions.solutionHtml:
All best-suited components
  • The kidneys have a special feedback mechanism that links changes in the sodium chloride concentration at the macula densa with the control of renal arteriolar resistance and autoregulation of GFR.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall,14th Edition, Page Number 339.

questions.stemHtml: The image below describes the structure of the juxtaglomerular apparatus in kidneys.Select the correct type of cells for the A and B marked in the image in red color?
questions.solutionHtml:
Juxtaglomerular cells----A, macula densa----B
  • The tubuloglomerular feedback mechanism has two components that act together to control GFR: (1) an afferent arteriolar feedback mechanism; and (2) an efferent arteriolar feedback mechanism. These feedback mechanisms depend on special anatomical arrangements of the juxtaglomerular complex.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall,14th Edition, Page Number 339-340.

questions.stem: The macula densa cells can control the renal blood flow in afferent arterioles and regulate the release of renin from juxtaglomerular cells in afferent and efferent arterioles.Select the best possible explanation of macula densa cell’s sensitivity to above-stated functions?

options.label: A
options.text: Reduction in GFR → reduction in flow rate in loop of Henle → increased reabsorption of sodium chloride in ascending loop of Henle → reduces concentration of sodium chloride in macula densa

options.label: B
options.text: Decreases resistance to blood flow in the afferent arterioles →raises glomerular hydrostatic pressure → normalizes GFR

options.label: C
options.text: Both A and B are best possible explanations

options.label: D
options.text: Both A and B are inappropriate explanations

questions.answerText: Both A and B are best possible explanations
questions.solutionHtml:
Both A and B are best possible explanations
  • The decreased GFR slows the flow rate in the loop of Henle, causing increased reabsorption of the percentage of sodium and chloride ions delivered to the ascending loop of Henle and thereby reducing the concentration of sodium at the Macula densa cells.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall,14th Edition, Page Number 340.

questions.stem: The glomerular filtration rate is the product of the average filtration rate of every single nephron multiplied by the number of nephrons in both kidneys. The glomerular filtration rate is determined by the balance of hydrostatic and colloid osmotic pressure.Select the correct factors that promote glomerular filtration?

options.label: A
options.text: The hydrostatic pressure of glomerular capillary

options.label: B
options.text: Oncotic pressure of the glomerular capillary

options.label: C
options.text: The hydrostatic pressure of Bowman's capsule

questions.answerText: The hydrostatic pressure of glomerular capillary
questions.solutionHtml:
The hydrostatic pressure of glomerular capillary
  • Hydrostatic pressure is the pressure produced by a fluid against a surface. The blood inside the glomerulus creates glomerular hydrostatic pressure which forces fluid out of the glomerulus into the glomerular capsule.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall, 14th Edition, Page Number 331-333.

questions.stem: Myogenic mechanisms regulate the maintenance of a relatively constant renal blood flow and glomerular filtration rate. The mechanism is dependent on the ability of blood vessels to resist stretching during increased arterial pressure.Select the essential elements in the myogenic mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Small arterioles respond to increased wall stretch by relaxation of the vascular smooth muscle

options.label: B
options.text: The stretch of the vascular wall allows increased movement of calcium ions from the extracellular fluid into the cells causing them to contract

options.label: C
options.text: This contraction prevents excessive stretch of the vessel and, at the same time, by raising vascular resistance, helps prevent excessive increases in renal blood flow and the GFR when arterial pressure increases

questions.solutionHtml:
Both B and C
  • Another mechanism that contributes to the maintenance of a relatively constant renal blood flow and GFR is the ability of individual blood vessels to resist stretching during increased arterial pressure, referred to as the myogenic mechanism.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall,14th Edition, Page Number 341.

questions.stem: The patient of 34 years reported pain in back muscles over the past 10 days. The patient gave H/O of lifting a heavy load. Examination revealed lumbar spine sprained. The physician prescribed NSAID for 5 days.Select the correct form of NSAID on the GFR of the patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
GFR reduces
  • In the case of the 34-year-old patient with a lumbar spine sprain, the use of NSAIDs for a short period of 5 days is reducing GFR.
  • NSAIDs block the synthesis of prostaglandins, thus reducing their dilation capability on the afferent arteriole, reducing GFR.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall,14th Edition, Page Number 338.

questions.stem: The kidney maintains a constant renal blood flow rate between 80 and 180 mmHg. The kidney can partly autoregulate this pressure by responding to changes detected by stretch receptors.Select the correct name of the mechanism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Myogenic mechanism
  • Another mechanism that contributes to the maintenance of a relatively constant renal blood flow and GFR is the ability of individual blood vessels to resist stretching during increased arterial pressure, referred to as the myogenic mechanism.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology by John E. Hall, Michael E. Hall edition 14th, page number 341.

questions.stem: Patient of age 23 years reported to a physician with nausea, vomiting, fatigue, flank pain, pain with urination, and visible blood in the urine, frothy urine for the past 12 days. The patient gave H/O taking sulfonamides for the treatment of sore throat in the previous week. Examination and urinalysis led to renal disease.Select the correct one?

options.label: B
options.text: Destruction of podocytes, and filtration membrane

questions.solutionHtml:
All correct
  • The nephritic syndrome is characterized by blood in the urine (especially Red blood cell casts with dysmorphic red blood cells) and a decrease in the amount of urine in the presence of hypertension.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.1540.

questions.stemHtml: Physiologists studied the permeability of different parts of the nephron. The image shows part of the nephron marked in 3 Number.Select the incorrect ?

options.label: A
options.text: Low permeability for sodium and chloride ions

questions.solutionHtml:
Water low permeability
  • Within the nephron of the kidney, the descending limb of the loop of Henle is the portion of the renal tubule constituting the first part of the loop of Henle.
  • It has low permeability for sodium and chloride ions, high permeability for water, and moderate permeability for urea.


Ganong’s Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.1551

questions.stem: Which of the following provides the most accurate measure of GFR?
questions.solutionHtml:
Inulin clearance
  • Inulin clearance provides the most accurate measure of GFR (glomerular filtration rate).
  • Inulin is a fructose polysaccharide that is freely filtered by the glomerulus and is not secreted, absorbed, or metabolized by the tubules. Therefore, the clearance of inulin is equal to the GFR.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 391.

questions.stem: Renal medullary hyperosmolarity is due to:
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • In juxtamedullary nephrons with longer loops and thin ascending limbs, the osmotic gradient is spread over a greater distance and the osmolality at the tip of the loop is greater.
  • This is because the thin ascending limb is relatively impermeable to water but permeable to Na+ and Cl-


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 655-56.

questions.stem: Which of the following does not form a filtration barrier in nephrons:
questions.solutionHtml:
Mesangium
  • The mesangium is a part of the glomerulus that provides structural support to the capillaries and helps to regulate blood flow. It does not form a filtration barrier in the nephrons.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 386.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old man has been vomiting to the point where he has become hypovolemic, as evidenced by an accompanying decrease in blood pressure and a feeling of light-headedness. The kidneys respond by reducing urinary volume flow, thus limiting the potential extent of hypovolemia. Increases in the plasma levels of which of the following hormones will bring about the most dramatic decrease in urinary volume flow rate?
questions.solutionHtml:
Arginine vasopressin (ADH)
  • Increases in plasma levels of arginine vasopressin, or ADH, lead to water reabsorption by the collecting ducts, decreasing urine output.
  • In the scenario described, the hypovolemia caused by vomiting would stimulate the release of ADH, which would cause the kidneys to reduce the urinary volume flow rate and conserve water. This would help to maintain blood volume and pressure and prevent further dehydration.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 660.
